newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher led by blue chips.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Sunday, boosted by a strong performance by blue chips on the Maof index, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.77 percent, or 2.21 points, to 289.90 on heavy all-share turnover of 255 million shekels against 207 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.30 percent higher at 299.59.
Traders said the session opened with a decline of 0.7 percent in the Mishtanim but during the day the market recovered.
"The market refuses to decline as more investors want to get in," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets. "There is lots of money looking for shares and the market is not selective at all."
Traders said Maof shares were the main winners while small-cap stocks traded on the Karam index closed almost unchanged.
Weiss predicted the positive trend, barring any dramatic developments on the political front, was likely to continue.

Earlier on Sunday, Israel's High Court rejected a petition demanding that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu be indicted for fraud in a decision his aides said closed the door on a six-month government corruption scandal.
"Today's court ruling added to investors' confidence and there is less uncertainty now," Weiss said.
Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities said: "The general public is not returning to the market yet but some are already testing the water."
Kolka said investors had shown confidence the May consumer price index (CPI) would be relatively low.
The CPI figure, released on Sunday after the end of the trading day, rose 0.5 percent -- well under analysts' expectations of 0.7 to 0.9 percent.

"Usually activity is relatively low ahead of the CPI release but the volume was very high today. If the CPI is lower than 0.7 percent the Bank of Israel will lower its key lending rate," Kolka said before May's figure was announced.
The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce its July monetary programme, including interest rates, on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 823 agorot on volume of 18.6 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which climbed 1.5 percent to 543 agorot on turnover of 17.4 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 0.75 percent to 20,538 agorot on volume of 14.1 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
